newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 3.

text.p: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times
Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- NORWICH UNION HOPES TO RAISE 2 BILLION STERLING FROM
FLOAT

Life assurance group Norwich Union is seeking a stock market floatation next year which it hopes will raise an estimated 2 billion stg. The move will be the first by a UK life assurer to abandon mutual ownership, and may put pressure on others to follow suit. However, two major rivals, Standard Life and Scottish Widows, have both stressed their commitment to mutual status.
-- HIGH STREET GROUPS USING LOW PAY SUPPLIERS IN UK

An investigation by the Financial Times newspaper has revealed that high street retailers are using British-based clothing suppliers which pay their staff as little as 1.50 stg an hour. A number of retailers have said they will investigate the claims, after codes of practice relating to pay and conditions were introduced in the industry in response to concern from campaign groups and charities.
-- NATIONAL GRID FACES 1 BILLION STG CUT IN REVENUE

National Grid, the operator of the electricity transmission system in England and Wales, is expected to be ordered by industry regulator Offer to cut its prices by 20 per cent. The cuts, due to run from next April until March 2002, would cost Grid about 1 billion stg in lost revenue. The group may challenge the order before the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
-- LEX CREATES 3,000 JOBS IN CAR REPAIR SECTOR

Automotive retailing group Lex Service is to invest 50 million stg in a venture to establish the country's first national network of specialist vehicle accident repair centres. The venture, to be called Lex Bodycentres, will have 50 specialised centres and is expected to create 3,000 jobs over the next two to three years. The first centre will be opened in Glasgow on Friday.
-- NEWSPAPERS TARGETED FOR RECYCLING PLAN

Environment secretary John Gummer has targeted the newspaper industry in his campaign to promote more recycling. Following the launch earlier this week of a landfill tax, Gummer has said he now intends to reach agreement before the end of this year with publishers and paper makers over targets for the use of recycled newsprint.
-- VODAFONE RESISTS MARKET DOWNTURN

Cellular phone group Vodafone has reported only moderate growth in the third quarter of 1996, but still retains its position as leader in the UK market. Vodafone has revised its estimate of the size of the UK cellphone market by 2000, from between 10 million and 14 million to a lower figure between 8 million and 10 million subscribers. Vodafone currently has 2.65 million subscribers, with almost 1 million on its digital network. The group's main rivals, Cellnet, has 2.54 million subscribers, with 654,000 of them connected digitally.
-- MONOPOLY REFERRAL COULD HIT GAS OUTPUT

Gas industry regulator Clare Spottswoode has warned that if British Gas refers its current dispute with Ofgas to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, the company would have no incentive to increase its productivity. Spottswoode suggested that the management of British Gas' monopoly pipeline operator, TransCo, would be left 'on hold', as the company would have to appeal to the MMC on the basis of its present productivity.
-- MARKETS WELCOME KPN'S A$2 BILLION OFFER FOR TNT

A $2 billion Australian (1 billion stg) approved bid by Dutch group KPN for the Australian transport and express delivery group TNT has been welcomed by the markets, with shares in both companies rising. The deal will create one of the world's top four - and Europe's largest - carriers in what the groups call 'time-sensitive distribution and logistics'.
-- TELEKOM PROPOSES DM3 BILLION PAYOUT

German state-owned telecoms operator Deutsche Telekom, which is due to be floated in Europe's largest privatisation, is expected to announce on Friday a dividend forecast of 3 billion deutschemarks (1.3 billion stg) for next year. The figure is double the DM1.5 billion it has said it will pay investors this year. A price range for shares in the floatation, which is expected to raise DM10 billion to DM15 billion, will be announced on October 22.
-- EUROTUNNEL BOARD LOOKS AT REFINANCING PACKAGE

Following a last-minute refinancing deal with its leading bankers, the board of Anglo-French channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel has met to discuss the deal. A final draft of the agreement, which will refinance Eurotunnel's 9 billion stg debts, will be circulated within the next few days prior to a formal signature on the terms.
